author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Elena Rybakina defeated two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 Saturday to win her first U.S. Open singles title. The victory gave the 27-year-old from Kazakhstan her third Grand Slam championship and ended Sabalenka’s 20-match winning streak at Flushing Meadows.

Rybakina took the first set before Sabalenka forced a decider. She regained control in the third, using her serve and first-strike power to pull away. The result denied Sabalenka a third consecutive U.S. Open crown and completed Rybakina’s run through the tournament after an ankle injury had threatened her participation.

The title follows Rybakina’s victories at Wimbledon in 2022 and the Australian Open earlier in 2026. She became the third woman this century to win both hard-court majors in the same season. The championship also places her at the top of the women’s rankings, the first player representing Kazakhstan to reach world No. 1, and carried a $5.5 million prize.
dek: Rybakina won 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 to claim her third major and end the defending champion’s 20-match Flushing Meadows streak.
headline: Elena Rybakina beats Aryna Sabalenka for first U.S. Open title
